title: Cost reporting templates and alert playbook (prototype notes)
content:
Context and goal:

This doc captures a compact prototype for: (A) a set of reusable cost-reporting CSV/JSON templates for customers to download, and (B) a decision/playbook for budget alerts that integrates with export flows. Primary goal is to unblock engineering + design on a first-pass export UX and an alerts UX that maps cleanly to cost centers and committed capacity.

Audience: product PM, UX, eng (backend + API), analytics, CS ops.

Constraints / assumptions:
- Must work for Hosted + Dedicated + Private views (same exported shape, with extra columns for private deployments when applicable).
- Exports should be producible via Console UI and Admin API (export job pattern).
- Customers expect CSV first (spreadsheet friendly) and JSON for programmatic ingestion.
- Alerts must be actionable: include links to export, to experiment history, and to recommend mitigations (e.g., enable caching, change batch size profile).

High level flows (text wireframes):

1) Export flow (Console) -> "Save & Download" modal
- Trigger: top-right "Export" button on Cost Center / Billing Overview / Budget page.
- Modal step 1: Select template (drop-down) [Recommended templates: Monthly P&L, Cost by Model + Route, Commit vs Overage, Token-level sample].
  - Each template has short description and estimated row count (based on query scope).
- Modal step 2: Filter scope (time range: presets + custom; teams / cost centers / projects; model family; deployment mode).
- Modal step 3: Output format (CSV | JSON | Parquet) and delivery (Download now | Email me when ready | S3 webhook).
- Modal step 4: Advanced: include raw request logs? include prompt/response hashes? include line-item attribution for cached tokens?
- Confirm -> kicks off export job; show job id, ETA, and link to Exports page where past exports are listed and re-runnable.

Minimal wireframe copy (console):
- Export modal header: "Export billing report"
- Template tile text: "Cost-by-Model (CSV) — summarizes spend by model and route. Useful for cost optimization and model-level chargebacks."

2) Export job landing page (Exports list)
- Columns: name, created_by, template, scope, rows_est, status, size, actions (download, re-run, cancel).
- Row actions: "Re-run with same filters", "Re-run with modifications", "Create subscription (recurring export)".
- Error handling: show first 3 errors inline (e.g., "private export requires SSO consent").

3) Alert creation flow (Budget alert wizard)
- Step 1: Choose scope (Cost center | Project | Team | Entire account).
- Step 2: Metric to watch (Spend forecast | Current month run rate | Token units | Request count).
- Step 3: Trigger condition (absolute threshold or percentage of budget). Support sliding windows (7d average, 24h peak).
- Step 4: Actions (Notify Slack channel / Email addresses / Create export snapshot / Auto-invoke model routing fallback).
- Step 5: Add runbook steps (optional free text or choose from template runbooks).
- Confirmation: generate testing preview: "If current trajectory continues you'll hit 85% in 4 days" with a small sparkline.

Alert UX details & messaging copy examples:
- Name: "Prod infra spend — U.S. Team"
- Trigger copy: "Spending > $20,000 in a 30-day window"
- Suggested action copy: "Export last 30 days (Cost-by-Model). Consider disabling non-prod dedicated pools or lowering burst cap."
- Notification card: include export link + quick buttons: [Export snapshot] [Acknowledge] [Open recommendations].

Templates (prototype canonical set) — header rows shown as CSV columns (short explanations in parens):
1) monthly-pnl.csv (high-level):
- date, account_id, cost_center, total_spend_usd, committed_discount_usd, net_spend_usd, credits_applied_usd, month_start, month_end
2) model-route-allocation.csv (detailed):
- timestamp, request_id, user_id, project_id, model_name, model_variant, route_name, tokens_input, tokens_output, billed_tokens, cpu_ms, gpu_ms, cost_usd, cache_hit (yes/no), quantization_profile, region

3) commit-versus-usage.csv (commit balancing):
- month, commitment_id, committed_amount_usd, usage_amount_usd, overage_amount_usd, carryover_credit_usd, utilization_pct

4) token-sampling.csv (for quality/reconcile):
- sample_timestamp, request_id, model_name, prompt_hash, response_hash, prompt_length, response_length, note

5) audit-export.json (structured audit for Private):
- recommended top-level keys: export_id, generated_at, scope, created_by, rows_count, checksum, encryption_used (yes/no), kms_key_id (if provided)

Export semantics notes / edge cases:
- Private exports must optionally redact PII and require an export-level consent checkbox for on-prem deployments.
- For very large ranges (>10M rows) we only include summary aggregates by default and offer raw logs as a separate "raw-logs" job via S3.
- Rows_est is computed via fast approximation; allow user to set "full detail" but surface higher ETA.
- When model variants are rolled out (canary), exports should include a column "variant_id" to attribute cost to rollout buckets.

Alert routing and integrations playbook (draft):
- Default notif channel: Owner + Billing Admin + Project Slack channel.
- If "Create export snapshot" selected: create an export job with the "Cost-by-Model" template scoped to 30d, attach job link to the alert notification.
- For "Auto-scale fallback": call routing API to switch traffic to a lower-cost variant (policy must be pre-provisioned by infra/engr).

Backlog & prioritization (MVP -> v1):
- MVP (must have): Export modal + templates, Exports page (list & download), Budget alert wizard with Email + Slack notifications, ability to attach export snapshot to alert.
- v1 (nice to have): Recurring/ scheduled exports, API for programmatic retrieval + webhooks, advanced filtering by model-version and rollout buckets, export encryption key selection.
- v2: On-demand aggregation windows (hourly rolls), connect to BI tooling via native connector (BigQuery / Snowflake), row-level encryption for Private.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Console: user can export CSV for given cost center for last 30 days and download file under 2 minutes for typical 100k-row job.
- Exports list shows job status and allows re-run.
- Budget alert fires and creates a linked export snapshot in notifications (link resolves).
- Exports respect RBAC: only users with Billing View role can download cost exports.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we let exports include prompt/response text by default (privacy risk)? Proposed: default to hashes; customer can opt-in per-export to include raw content with consent.
- Default frequency for recurring exports? Weekly end-of-week recommended by finance.
- Should alert actions include a "temporary commit cap" adjustment (billing implications)? Legal / finance to weigh in.
- Retention policy for generated exports: keep for 90 days in Console; longer retention only via customer push to their S3.

Implementation notes for eng:
- Provide Export Jobs API v1: POST /exports {template, scope, format, delivery} -> returns job_id. GET /exports/{job_id} for status + download url.
- Export job runs on analytics cluster; large-job routing to async workers with presigned S3 upload.
- Alerts: reuse metrics infra (billing metrics) and schedule rule evaluation via existing scheduler; include exported_snapshot_id in alert payload.

QA checklist for release:
- RBAC tests for every scope (account, cost center, project).
- Export correctness test: random spot-check rows vs analytics query.
- Export performance test (100k rows local, 5M rows large path).
- Notification payload test: deep link to export and runbook insertion.

Prototype UI tasks for Design:
- Create small template picker micro-interaction (hover -> short tooltip + estimated rows).
- Create alert preview microcard with sparkline and recommended actions.
- Small skeleton for Exports page with progressive disclosure for large jobs.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally pragmatic (spreadsheet-first). Focus on not over-building: customers have BI teams who will consume CSVs.
- Priority is linking alerts to immediate action (exports + recommended mitigations).

Next steps / owners:
- PM (Ava) to finalize template column sets with finance by 2025-01-21.
- Eng (Diego) to prototype Export Jobs API stub by 2025-01-28.
- Design (Priya) to produce 3 small wireframe mocks for the modal + alert card by 2025-02-03.

Changelog:
- 2025-01-14: initial draft created.
- 2025-01-31: added export templates and backlog section (Ava).
- 2025-02-04: updated alerts playbook and QA checklist (Diego).
